results.reason: Issue 3 contrasts MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester) with Schedule §1.1 (shipment from Supplier's plant). It explains that transit time changes whether Verdane is late, which affects time-of-essence cancellation and cover. It also covers risk passing at shipment and invoicing keyed to the shipment date.
The fix conforms Schedule §1.1 to the MSA (delivery at Rochester) and adds an order-of-precedence clause stating the MSA prevails.

Issue 2 identifies MSA §4.3 as worldwide exclusivity over all housings and similar components. It contrasts this with Term Sheet §§3.1–3.3 (Series 7, U.S. only), explains the lock-in effect on Harlow's sourcing, and recommends narrowing to Series 7 Housings in the U.S.

Issue 6 cites §15.2: Supplier may assign freely, while Customer needs consent. It flags the risk of assignment to a competitor or thinly capitalized entity and exposure of confidential specifications. It recommends requiring Harlow's consent, or at minimum a termination right and exclusivity release on assignment or change of control.
Issue 1 explains that Amendment §§2.1–2.2 cut the §11.2 carve-outs to willful misconduct only, capping gross negligence and the IP indemnity. It recommends restoring the original §11.2 exclusions.
The memo states the IP indemnity is now capped at the prior 12 months' fees. It lists the original §11.2 exclusions as gross negligence, willful misconduct and the §10.1 IP indemnity.
The memo states Term Sheet §§3.1–3.3 limits exclusivity to Series 7 Housings within the U.S. and uses this as the baseline for comparison with §4.3.
